instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: During the First World War, Britain was a leading Allied power, establishing the Royal Air Force and introducing conscription in 1916. The war was justified through liberal principals and commitment to France, but also served to provide domestic political unity. Suffrage — which had previously been tied to property — was granted to all men over 21 in 1918, and for women in 1928.

atoms.a: For which reasons did the UK participate in World War I?
b: ++liberal principles like defending small nations and the rule of law

atoms.a: Until 1918 and 1928, what aspect other than gender did suffrage depend on?

atoms.text: Over the course of the Second World War, Britain endured heavy bombing during The Blitz, suffered over 60,000 civilian deaths, and faced strict rationing and shortages of food, clothing, and everyday goods. WW1's patriotism was replaced by a serious, determined attitude, knowing that Adolf Hitler had to be stopped by force. Prime Minister Winston Churchill appeared as a key national figure, remembered today for his efforts in conquering Nazi Germany.

suffrage – Wahlrecht

hint.label: Vocab

atoms.a: Patriotism was a common British motive for and during World War I. What shaped World War II?

atoms.text: After the war was won, Britain was amongst the founding members of the United Nations in 1945 and in 1973 they joined the United Communities (UC) which would later become the European Union (EU). In 1948, the roots of the National Health Service (NHS), also a culturally significant system, were established and later expanded. Politically, the UK underwent controversial change during Margaret Thatcher's time as Prime Minister from 1979 to 1990, which, for example, restricted social spending.

atoms.a: Which is a key British Institution founded in 1948?

atoms.b: At the peak of the empire, about 25 % of the world was under British ((rule)). The Era of the Empire was certainly marked by expansion, wealth and power for Britain, but also by brutality as well as oppression and ((exploitation)) of the colonies and their people. The world wars significantly weakened Britain's ((economy)) and military powers, and in the years to come, more and more former colonies gained ((independence)). The handing over of Hong Kong to China in 1997 marks the end of the empire.

In 1949, the Commonwealth of Nations was formally established. Between the 1950s and 1970s, most remaining ((colonies)) became independent but joined the Commonwealth ((voluntarily)). Today, it is a post-empire network made up of 56 independent countries, led only symbolically by Britain's ((monarch)).
